She accepts the thanks with a modest smile and turns it toward the introduction she wants.

“I'm glad it helped. Perhaps you could introduce me to someone willing to hear about my work? Only an introduction; I can make the request myself.”

The useful map gives her a better opening than a demand would. She tries to make the next favor seem small and continuous with the help already received, while watching whether the traveler actually wants to continue. If the answer is no, she will need another approach. She has acquired an occasion to ask, not an enforceable claim over the traveler, and she does not announce cooperation before hearing the reply.

She lets the failed favor drop rather than thanking the traveler on their own behalf. Pressing the map as a debt now would expose how little she has supplied.

“Then I haven't saved you any trouble. What would make an introduction worth your time?”

She asks the question pleasantly, but the change costs her the easy appearance of being owed something. She wants to discover an opening that the traveler actually values, without yet claiming she can provide it. Another refusal may make this person a poor use of her time. For now, she keeps the desired introduction as a proposal and looks for information instead of pretending the rejected benefit created an obligation.

Serena stops before beginning the animation and turns on the follower with a frustrated demand.

“You insist on staying like this, and now I can't even put one body to work. Tell me what would persuade you to let me change this arrangement.”

She wants relief from the cost without simply surrendering her hold, but there is no spare control to spend on both wishes. For the moment, she suspends the corpse-crew plan and tries to negotiate with the person consuming the resource. Her impatience does not make the follower's refusal disappear. She keeps the shovel available for ordinary work if bargaining fails, resentful that a supposedly useful servant has become the obstacle to getting anything done.

Serena begins the admitted puppet spell on the excavated body, using the spare control rather than releasing the difficult follower.

“One worker first. Then perhaps I can get something done without another argument.”

She keeps the planned crew small because the available margin is small. The prospect of having the body do ordinary labor is attractive precisely because she is tired of supplying the effort herself. She does not expand the attempt into an army or declare the spell successful before seeing its effect. Maintaining the follower remains a cost she has chosen to carry; this time it leaves one usable opening, and she attempts to use it before that opening is consumed by another demand.

Serena addresses the third adult instead of answering the guards' demand for everything. She has seen enough to consider the limited bargain real, though that does not make these people allies.

“Route logistics. That is what you offered to exchange, and that is what I will discuss. The other information stays out of it. Confirm the release terms.”

She prepares to supply the narrower category if the terms hold, trying to turn her knowledge into an exit without giving away every protected detail. Fear makes the offer valuable, but she is still bargaining over its boundary. She does not profess a new loyalty, confess unspecified crimes or assume the guards have agreed before anyone replies.

Serena keeps the offer at the level of terms and asks the third adult to demonstrate the authority being claimed.

“You can promise release. Can you actually undo these bindings? Show me that before you ask what I know.”

She avoids answering the guards' broad demand and leaves open a smaller exchange. Giving away the useful part first might remove the only bargaining piece she has without changing her position at all. Her caution is strained rather than fearless; she wants the offer to be credible. For now, she requests evidence and withholds the protected personal information. A demonstrated way out could change the negotiation, but she does not invent that evidence merely because she needs it.
